A Warm Welcome
Welcome to Chard Prep School, a unique independent school in South Somerset, bordering East Devon and West Dorset.
Our children learn in beautiful historic Grade II* listed buildings steeped in rich educational heritage, while our talented teachers, caring support staff and dedicated parents create a tight-knit family atmosphere in which all children thrive.
Academic excellence is our guiding principle, with small classes and specialist teachers ably catering to children’s individual needs, and there are well-trodden pathways from Chard Prep School to leading grammar schools and local senior schools.
However, we believe that the key to academic success is a happy, confident child, and at Chard Prep, exemplary pastoral care is at the heart of the school. Our children realise their own potential because they are given the space, time and guidance to explore who they are as individuals. We strive to nurture well-rounded young people who are aware of others’ needs and ideas as well as their own, and who go on to make positive contributions to society.
We celebrate pupils’ achievements in all areas of the curriculum. Our children create fantastic artwork in our art studio and make stellar progress in weekly swimming and in inter-school sports fixtures. They display bravery in treading the boards of our chapel in musical and theatrical performances, and concoct original ideas in our Science lab, home of Squishy the Axolotl.
Chard Prep School is a relaxed and friendly environment, where children are eager to learn. There is room for creative experiment and challenge with dedicated staff who truly listen to the child. So come on in, join our community and experience the magic!

Our School Values
Children who are Ready and Resilient for Tomorrow
At Chard Prep School, we believe in shaping more than just academic achievers. Everything we do is driven by our Values
Empathy
We foster a compassionate community where every pupil feels seen, heard, and valued. Empathy is at the core of our interactions, ensuring that no one walks alone on their journey
Courage
We encourage pupils to step out of their comfort zones, take risks, and embrace challenges. Courage fuels growth, and we believe in nurturing bold thinkers who fearlessly explore new horizons
Respect for Others
Our pupils learn that respect extends beyond mere tolerance. It’s about celebrating diversity, appreciating different perspectives, and treating everyone with kindness, politeness and dignity
Integrity
Honesty, accountability, and ethical behaviour are non-negotiable. We instil integrity in our pupils, knowing that their character matters as much as their academic, artistic and sporting achievements
Together, we are preparing children not just for senior schools but for a life of purpose, impact, and positive change
Chard Prep School Mission – Why We do what we do
Preparing Tomorrow’s Leaders
At Chard Prep School, we’re committed to nurturing well-rounded, resilient, and confident pupils. Our unique approach focuses on:
Wellbeing & Confidence: We prioritise physical, mental and emotional health, fostering a positive environment where students feel supported, empowered, and ready to face challenges.
Progression to Top Senior Schools: We prepare our pupils for success by providing rigorous academics, personalised support, and guidance to secure placements in leading senior schools.
Accessible Education: Our inclusive approach ensures that every pupil has equal opportunities to learn and grow, regardless of their background or abilities.
Resilience: We teach adaptability, problem-solving, and perseverance, equipping pupils to thrive in an ever-changing world.
Preparedness for Change: We emphasise flexibility, critical thinking, and creativity, enabling pupils to embrace change confidently.
Chard Prep School Strategy – What we do
Our focus areas include:
Pastoral Care: Providing dedicated support systems that cater to the individual
Educational Excellence / Well Roundedness: Ensuring that academic rigour and physical education complements a broad range of subjects and extracurricular activities to foster intellectual curiosity and versatility.
Nurturing Creative Environment: Cultivating creativity through an engaging curriculum that encourages innovation and self-expression.
Accessible Education: Making quality education available to the wider community.
Chard Prep School Culture – How we implement our Vision
How: Implementing Our Vision
Wellbeing Initiatives: Approaches that promote physical and mental health, resilience, and self-awareness.
Tailored Academic Programmes: Implement a curriculum that balances excellence with holistic development, encouraging pupils to explore diverse interests.
Creative Learning Spaces: Create environments that inspire creativity, collaboration, and critical thinking, fostering a love for learning.
Financial Assistance: Ensure accessibility by providing scholarships, bursaries, guidance on grants, advanced and flexible payment options for families.
Staff Training: Continuously train our educators to deliver high-quality education, safeguarding and support.
Modelling: Expecting and demanding that our Staff, Governors and Parents model the behaviours in school that we expect of our pupils.
Chard Prep School Behaviours
All behaviours should align with and reinforce the Chard Prep School Values. Behaviours should be demonstrated and modelled, by:
Further details may be found in the pupils contract, parents contract, Governors Behaviour Agreement and the Staff Handbook.

School History
Chard Prep School has a long and unique history. Its main building is a beautiful sixteenth-century town house, which is listed Grade II*, putting it in the top 5% of buildings of historic and architectural importance. Built in 1583 for a wealthy local merchant, John Symes, the house was donated to the town of Chard as a Grammar School by his successors in 1671, and there has been a school on the site continuously ever since. It remained the town’s grammar school until 1890, when it became a public boarding school. In 1972 the present school was established, as an independent co-educational preparatory school.
Over the years other adjacent buildings were added, including the thatched Elizabethan chapel, the eighteenth-century Monmouth House, also Grade II* listed, and more recently the gymnasium and a purpose built science laboratory. The school’s classes are named after figures who are prominent in the history of Chard and the school – Symes, Horner, Monmouth, Wyndham, Harris and Cerdic.
Chard School - Three Centuries of History
This comprehensive account of the three hundred years history of one of the oldest schools in Somerset, sponsored by the Old Cerdics Association, was written and researched by the eminent author and Old Cerdic Derrick Warren who spent his working life as a cartographic surveyor with the Ordnance Survey.First published amidst wide acclaim and media interest at the school’s Summer Fair in 2007 the story goes back to the very beginning in 1671 when William Symes gave his Manor Housein Chard to the Portreeve and Burgesses of the Borough ‘for the education and bringing up of youth in virtue and learning’. A second edition bringing the history right up to date, including some of the most difficult years in the school’s long history brought about by the global pandemic was published in 2021.
The book is available to purchase from the school at £18.00 to include p&p.
Please contact the Office Manager at office@chardprep.co.uk

Learning Support & Pastoral Care
Small Teaching Groups
In the Pre-School Nursery, the average teacher:pupil ratio is 1:6. Children with specific educational needs are therefore more easily identified and can be helped within the classroom by class and subject teachers, much more readily than in schools with larger class sizes.
Classroom Assistance
Classroom support from Teaching Assistants is available to teachers, especially in the Pre-Prep, to make teaching groups even smaller and more effective.
Assessment
All pupils are assessed, using teacher assessments - both written and digital standardised tests - at regular intervals, so that progress can be continually reviewed and evaluated.
Pastoral Care
At Chard Prep School, prioritising well-being is paramount, with teachers equipped with training in mindfulness programmes. We firmly believe that a child's success, both within and beyond the classroom, hinges on their sense of happiness and security in their environment. By inspiring children to seize the opportunities available at Chard Prep School, we aim to empower them to develop into confident and well-rounded young individuals.

Safeguarding
At Chard Prep School, we are committed to safeguarding children. It is the duty and responsibility of everyone to safeguard and promote the welfare of children. We recognise the needs and wishes of every child and these will be put first. Safeguarding children means protecting them from abuse or neglect. Getting the right support in place as early as possible and creating an environment in which children and young people feel safe and healthy is our priority. We all have a personal responsibility to notice when a child or young person may be at risk of harm and pass our concerns to someone who can act to protect them.
Safeguarding Statement
Operation Encompass is a unique Police and Education early intervention safeguarding partnership which ensures that a child’s school is informed, prior to the start of the next school day, that there has been a domestic abuse incident to which the child has been exposed, and which might then have an impact on them in school.
Each school is informed of all such incidents that police are called to, not just those where an offence can be identified or those which are graded as high risk. The partnership recognises that all domestic abuse incidents can be harmful to children. Information will only be shared with the school by the police where it is identified that a young person was present anywhere in the home. This knowledge allows the school to provide immediate early intervention through silent or overt support dependent upon the needs and wishes of the child.
A nominated member of staff, known as a Key Adult, has been trained to liaise with the police. At Chard Prep our Key Adult is the Designated Safeguarding Lead, Mrs Sibley. She will be able to use information that has been shared with her, in confidence, to ensure that the school makes provision for possible difficulties experienced by children or their families. The Key Adult will keep this information confidential and will only share it on a need-to-know basis, for instance, to teaching staff for the child. It will not be shared with other school students.
If you would like some more information about it, you can view this online at www.operationencompass.org

pageCache.pageTitle: Chard Prep School — Friends of Chard Prep School
pageCache.text:
Friends of Chard Prep School
Chard Prep School has a very active and enthusiastic ‘Friends’ organisation, which organises a diverse range of social and fundraising activities throughout the year, which include the Christmas Fair and the Summer Fair, film afternoons, cake sales, coffee mornings and the annual pantomime trip.
Who are the ‘Friends’ of Chard Prep School?
All parents, teachers, governors and helpers are Friends of Chard Prep School but they are represented by a committee of parents who have volunteered their help. The Committee is made up of a Chairperson, Secretary and Treasurer together with up to ten other members, who will hopefully be representative of all age groups across the school.
What do the ‘Friends’ of Chard Prep School do?
1. Develop more extended relationships between staff, parents and others associated with Chard Prep School.
2. Engage in fundraising and organising of social events, the proceeds of which assist in the provision of such facilities, opportunities and items of education which the committee, in consultation with the Head, feel appropriate to advance the overall education of the pupils of Chard Prep School i.e. the icing on an already delicious cake!
How have funds been spent in recent years?
iPads for the children and staff to use in school
Maintenance of the Astroturf
Contribution towards school plays
Contribution to themed days at school
New chairs in the IT lab
A new PA system and microphone
New cookers/hobs/baking & cooking equipment
New musical instruments
New sandpit for the playground
Contribution towards Pre-Prep Outdoor Classroom
Contribution towards travel for Forest School
Without everyone’s support these amazing achievements for the school simply wouldn’t have been possible… Thank you!
Would you like to get involved?
New committee members are always welcome and even if you don’t feel you have the time to become a committee member, we are always looking for ‘Friends’ friends’: people who we can call upon to man the teapot, or help with a stall at the Summer and Christmas Fairs. Any help is always very much appreciated, as they say… ’many hands make light work!’
If you would like to join the Friends, help in any way or have any suggestions for the committee please do get in touch via email – friendsofchardschool@hotmail.com

pageCache.pageTitle: Chard Prep School — Head of School
pageCache.text:
Meet the Head of School
Chard Prep School is an amazing place. Something about the history, the small class sizes and relationships between staff and families gets into your whole being. I want that to thrive under my leadership. I want children to be excited and happy about coming to school each day. I want to help create a lifelong love of learning and give them the best possible chance of success in whatever area they choose.
My educational philosophy is led by a desire for all children to fulfil their potential. I fully believe that schools should be a place of wonder, excitement and curiosity and provide experiences and teaching that supports children in creating their own futures based on personal aspirations. Education should develop the ‘whole’ child. Alongside knowledge, teaching should support children to learn about morality and help them to develop their own personality. Effective education enables children to discover and develop their own values, even when sometimes conflicting with traditional ones. Pupils need hands-on experiences and opportunities to think critically, make connections, find deeper meanings and master concepts.
Becky PieleszHead of School
